chapter: Lee Collins and the riverboat Washington
title: Martin Cole, Claiborne Williamson and Benny Turner on jitney jobs
summary: They discuss Martin Cole on the boat, and Benny Turner and the hard jitney jobs.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: What did Martin Cole play by the way?

Well we had Martin Cole on the boat with us. He had got shot in his stomach one time and we used him on the boat, you know, short trip. Then he left and then he went out there fooling around with Claiborne Williamson, he was running his band while he was in the Navy down there. I was waiting for Buckaroo. That's a piano tune. That's a piano tune with David Williamson.
You know we were talking to Benny Turner and he told us to play with Williamson too and his piano when he was in the Navy.
No I played with Benny too, that's my boy. We used to work for the, across the river.
When did you work with them?
You didn't work in La Vida, huh?

Yeah I'd go there handing them. Yeah I went down there but them jobs was too hard. Yeah, them old jittery lad handing them, smoking them. I used to go by there and work at somebody's place. I'd go there and work in somebody's place, you understand what I mean? But not all that plan, you understand me?
No, that's really hard work according to Benny.
Yeah Benny Turner stayed there, because he didn't do nothing with the car, but he's great, he's great. He's great.
You like the way he's been? Mm-hmm. Yeah. Mm-hmm.
Who that? He played accompaniment, huh? Yeah, yeah, he, can fill in.
But you see them old, the jittery job, it makes you lazy. You gonna try to make less as you can, you can save yourself.
